terminal_record.description_short: The supplied record alleges a 2025 leak investigation targeting Gina Haspel; the packet does not verify that one was opened.
terminal_record.description_medium: The frozen record alleges that the Trump administration opened a classified-leak investigation of former CIA Director Gina Haspel in March 2025, framing it as retaliation. The packet provides no supporting source or case details. A July 2025 Federalist article discusses a proposal to investigate Haspel over Russia-related issues, but does not report the alleged March leak probe. This remains an internal, unverified allegation.
terminal_record.description_long: The frozen record alleges that the Trump administration opened a classified-leak investigation of former CIA Director Gina Haspel on March 20, 2025, over leaks said to have damaged President Trump. It frames the alleged inquiry as retaliation and says critics linked it to Haspel’s earlier handling of intelligence assessments and the Ukraine whistleblower matter. None of those asserted connections is established by the supplied packet: it identifies no agency announcement, case number, charge, named source, or contemporaneous report confirming that a leak investigation was opened. A July 28, 2025 Federalist article reports that Peter Schweizer raised questions about Haspel and argues in its headline that she should be investigated over Russia-related matters. That later commentary does not document a March leak inquiry, and its topic is distinct from the record’s alleged classified-leak probe. This draft preserves the supplied claim as an allegation for internal review. Its date and all attributed conduct remain unverified; do not present them as findings, charges, or proof of retaliation. Before publication, establish whether an official or credible report identifies a specific investigation and supports the claimed subject and date.

terminal_record.title: April 2025 Trump Administration Plan Proposed Cutting the CDC Budget by More Than 40%
terminal_record.description_short: CNN reported an April 10 internal plan proposed a CDC budget reduction of more than 40%; the draft could change and was not an enacted cut.
terminal_record.description_medium: An internal federal health-agency document dated April 10, 2025, proposed reducing the CDC budget by more than 40%, CNN reported on April 16. CNN said the draft could still be finalized with changes and would consolidate health programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. This corrected card concerns a proposal, not a March cut already in effect or proof that every surveillance program named in the original synopsis ended.
terminal_record.description_long: CNN reported on April 16, 2025, that an internal Trump administration document dated April 10 outlined a proposed reduction of more than 40% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s budget. The document also previewed a broader restructuring of federal health agencies and consolidation of programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. CNN reported that the plan could still be finalized with changes and described the reductions as what would happen “if enacted as is.” The evidence supports a proposed budget action; it does not show that the CDC had already received a 40% reduction in March. Nor does the accessed reporting substantiate that every program named in the original synopsis—including outbreak-detection grants, chronic-disease programs, global surveillance across 49 countries, and state emergency-preparedness agreements—was eliminated by this same proposal. This card therefore focuses on the April 10 proposal and leaves implementation unresolved. It does not combine the proposal, agency layoffs, and program closures into one completed event. The percentage is CNN’s description of the administration’s plan, not a final appropriation or an independently audited spending change.

terminal_record.title: Unverified Claim of an April 2025 Family-Separation Reinstatement
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied record alleges an April 2025 return to family separation; packet sources describe detention or deportation and do not verify that claim.
terminal_record.description_medium: The frozen synopsis alleges that the administration reinstated zero-tolerance family separation on April 1, 2025, separating thousands of parents and children and prosecuting parents. The packet does not establish those claims. Its AP item concerns Alien Enemies Act deportation flights, while the April Guardian report describes family detention, a distinct practice. The allegations remain unverified and are retained only for internal drafting.
terminal_record.description_long: The frozen synopsis alleges that the Trump administration reinstated its 2018 zero-tolerance family-separation policy on April 1, 2025. It claims that parents and children were deliberately separated as a deterrence measure, that thousands of families were affected, and that parents faced criminal prosecution. It further attributes an acknowledgment of intentional separation to the administration and says pediatricians and child-welfare experts warned of psychological harm. These are supplied allegations, not established findings in this packet. The AP source concerns Alien Enemies Act deportation flights. The April Guardian report describes family detention at Karnes and Dilley; detention does not establish that parents and children were separated from one another. The packet contains no same-event source confirming formal reinstatement, separations, the quantity, prosecution, attributed acknowledgment, or the quoted expert response. This internal draft keeps the supplied account visible for reconciliation while marking every central allegation unverified. It does not treat detention or deportation as proof of the claimed separation policy, and it does not assign an impact score to an unestablished event.
